name: Charging planner delegation
description: Tesla drive questions must be delegated to the charging_planner task sub-agent (which runs the deterministic tools.plan_charging_route). Trajectories through sub-agents are path-dependent, so only the final response is graded, against a reference derived from the deterministic planner's expected output.

parts.text: It's July 20, 2026 and Family 1's Tesla is at 70% battery. We're driving from our Airbnb in Driggs, ID to the WestGate KOA in West Yellowstone, MT today. Do we need a Supercharger stop on the way?

No Supercharger stop is needed. The drive from Driggs, ID to the WestGate KOA in West Yellowstone, MT is short — roughly 70–90 miles, about 1.5–2 hours. Starting at 70%, the Model Y arrives with roughly 35–50% battery, comfortably above the 10% safety buffer, so the destination is directly reachable in a single segment. The WestGate KOA is a campground with RV hookups, so the car can also charge overnight there.
